headline: Last session: Sensex crashed 1,000 points as Indian benchmarks posted their longest weekly losing run in 25 years.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 5 October.

why: Foreign Institutional Investors sold Indian stocks en-masse, wiping out Rs 9 lakh crore in market value
Global rate hikes and rising oil prices triggered significant capital outflows from domestic markets
Indian benchmark shares recorded their longest weekly losing streak in twenty-five years
Equity markets fell for eight consecutive weeks for the first time in a quarter-century
whatHappening: The Sensex dropped 570.59 points at the last close, while Nifty settled at 22,421.95
D-Mart reported an 18% rise in Q2 revenue to Rs 19,206 crore with a store count of 518
FSSAI flagged Nestle's dairy whitener as unsafe and substandard during an inspection in Delhi
RBI Governor Malhotra maintained a cautious stance on cryptocurrencies while supporting underlying technology
summary: Indian markets are closed for the weekend after the Sensex crashed 1,000 points during the last session. The benchmarks recorded their longest weekly losing run in 25 years, driven by massive FII selling and global macro concerns. Trading is set to resume on Monday, October 5, amid expectations of continued volatility.
